constants.registry: SI 2019 exact · CODATA 2022 · IAU 2012 B2 / 2015 B2–B3

coordinates: lm = log10(M/kg), lr = log10(R/m); log C = log10(2GM/(Rc²)), log Q = log10(ħ/(MRc)); S = d log R / d log M; p_eff = 1/S (M ∝ R^p_eff)

measured: planets: NASA Exoplanet Archive pscomppars, pl_bmassprov = "Mass" (true masses: no M sin i, no masses from an M–R relation)
local slopes and broken power law fitted to them, with block-bootstrap intervals
host stars: st_mass/st_rad — NOTE these are mostly model-derived (spectroscopy + isochrones or empirical relations), heterogeneous across papers
neutron stars from NICER (3 pulsars, 5 analyses)
model: Nauenberg 1972 white-dwarf mass–radius curve, μ_e = 2 (the atlas white-dwarf lab)
identity: C = 1 (R = 2GM/c²) and Q = 1 (R = ħ/(Mc)): definitions, not data
I_S = (1+S) log C + (1−S) log Q is constant along R ∝ M^S: a theorem (Lean: dilation_invariant, p = 1/S), not a finding
the allowed band C ≤ 1 ∧ Q ≤ 1 (Lean: allowed_masses, allowed_nonempty)
hypothetical: extrapolating any fitted slope outside its window
dilation trajectories M ∝ R^p drawn through a point
FBS3R rung lines: coordinates, not layers

planets.selection: pl_bmassprov = "Mass", finite radius and mass with both errors, no limit flags
planets.mr_covariance: not provided by the archive: ρ(M, R) = 0 assumed

hosts.selection: unique hosts with st_mass, st_rad and both errors; main-sequence cut 1/1.6 < R/M^0.8 < 1.6 (solar units)

white_dwarfs.caveat: transcribed from the papers named; three stars do not constrain a slope

neutron_stars.caveat: the M–R posteriors are correlated and not summarised by two intervals; two analyses of one pulsar share data. Three pulsars do not constrain a slope.

literature_model.src: Chen & Kipping 2017, ApJ 834, 17 (transcribed: verify against the paper)
